# Dragging a never-shown lazy tab out of the window closes its vessel

## Context

Measured in a downstream dock application whose panes load lazily: its `resolvePane` answers `{module: () => import(...)}`, the shape #20110 made work for runtime-added panes. Its layout restores two tabs in one stack, so only the active card materializes. Dragging the OTHER tab, whose card was never shown, past the app boundary opens a vessel that never receives the pane: the vessel closes again and the item returns to the dock.

The same gesture on an active tab, or on that tab once it has been shown, works. So does the same app with eagerly imported pane classes. The failing arm was red on the lazy build and green on the eager one, with the same steps (cold start with Log active beside the Editor, then a drag of the Editor tab past the boundary).

## The Problem

A lazy pane has no component until its card first shows. The card layout imports the module on activation (`layout.Card#loadModule`, idempotent per item), and the rail's reveal path does the same on first reveal. Nothing performs that first creation for the tear-out. At the detached terminal:
- `TearOut#onDockTearOutTerminal` commits `detachItem`.
- Its publication runs `Workspace#onTearOutDocumentChange`, which calls `tearOutHandlers.capturePane(itemId)`.
- `capturePane` asks the host's `resolvePane` → `Workspace#resolveLivePane(itemId)`. It searches `getDockHost().down({dockItemId})` for components, so a parked config is invisible to it, and it answers `null`.
- The commit then re-projects the item away, `adoptPane` has nothing to reparent, and the adoption compensates by retiring the vessel the gesture just opened.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority, `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsPanes.md` ("Reload, lazy creation and asynchronous work keep their ordinary meanings"): *"A lazy pane has no component instance until it first materializes. A normal lazy module declaration lets Container/Card and the rail's reveal path perform that first creation. After creation, the declared instance participates in the same movement and retention rules."* A tear-out is a movement whose first step needs the instance, and no creation path covers it.

- The parked config sits in the tab container's card body at its index, stamped `dockItemId` by `projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs` (`config.dockItemId = itemId`).
- The load primitive already exists and is reused by #20110's reconciler fix: `tab.getCardContainer().layout.loadModule(config, index)`. It joins a load already in flight, so a concurrent activation and a tear-out construct one instance.
- `TearOut#onDockTearOutTerminal` already returns `Boolean|Promise<Boolean>` and awaits an asynchronous publication, so an await before the commit fits its contract.

## The Fix

- Add an optional host seam to `TearOut`, a pane-preparation call for `itemId`. `onDockTearOutTerminal` awaits it before `applyOperation({operation: 'detachItem'})`, then re-checks that the admitted vessel is still the active one before committing. The reducer therefore runs on the document as it is after the load, never on one computed before it.
- `dock.Workspace` fills the seam. When `resolveLivePane(itemId)` finds nothing, it locates the parked config by `dockItemId` in its tabs' card bodies and awaits that body's `layout.loadModule(config, index)`. A host whose panes are eager pays nothing: the live pane is found first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A tab whose lazy card was never shown, dragged past the boundary, arrives in its vessel as a live pane, and its tab leaves the main window. A test in the engine's own harness fails on `dev` and passes with the fix.
- [x] An active tab's tear-out and an eager host's tear-out behave as before; the existing tear-out tests are unchanged and green.
- [x] One instance only: a tear-out racing the card's own activation load joins it (`loadModule`'s in-flight join), with no second construction.
- [x] A load that rejects leaves the gesture on its existing refusal path: the vessel retires and the item stays.
- [x] `DockLayoutsPanes.md` names the tear-out beside Container/Card and the rail's reveal as a first-creation path.

## Out of Scope

- Pop-out through the header action. It needs focus, which activates the card first.
- Lazily loading panes at boot: unchanged.

- #20110 / #20109: lazy panes added at runtime load in the tab-chrome reconciler.

during the load still wins. dock.Workspace fills it by loading the parked

so container.Base and the reconciler no longer each owe that cleanup.
